summary.text: 车 is a modern simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a wheeled vehicle. Its shape derives from the traditional graph’s cursive form.

formation.text: The traditional graph 車 pictures a vehicle as a whole. Early forms varied in the features shown; later forms selected and regularized some of them. The modern graph 车 derives from cursive 車.

history.text: Early oracle-bone and bronze forms of 車 varied in the vehicle features shown. Later forms selected and regularized some features. The curated oracle-bone, Western Zhou bronze, and seal-script examples illustrate different presentations; they are modern redrawings, not artifact photographs.
The modern simplified form 车 derives from cursive 車, attested by the Sui dynasty at the latest. It became a standard character in 1956. This change is distinct from earlier variation within 車.

uncertainties.text: Early forms varied, and the curated images are modern redrawings. Individual vehicle features in any one drawing should therefore be interpreted cautiously.
Early vehicle uses are identified by inscription references, but the cited evidence gives neither calendar dates for those inscriptions nor a precise earliest date for the graph.

senses.text: Oracle-bone examples use 車 for vehicles, and bronze examples include vehicles and war chariots. These attest early vehicle-related use but do not establish a calendar-dated first occurrence.
An oracle-bone example is identified as a place-name use. Its meaning and any connection to the vehicle sense are unresolved.

senses.gloss: wheeled machines; transporting by cart; cartload measure
senses.text: Later dictionaries record these uses, but the evidence does not date their emergence or establish a continuous development from the vehicle sense.
The common modern meaning includes vehicle and car.

limitations.text: The chronology and semantic links among later machinery, transport, and measure senses are unresolved, so no chain of development is proposed.

Some proposals treat the spoken word written 車 as borrowed from Indo-Iranian words for “wheel” or “chariot.” In that account, the graph was reused for another word because the words sounded alike or similar; the vehicle picture did not develop into that word’s meaning. The depicted vehicle’s spoken name is not independently established, so the proposed sound match remains disputed.
The traditional account that Xi Zhong made the vehicle in the Xia period is not independently confirmed by the cited evidence.

overview.text: 车 is the simplified form of 車, whose early forms pictured a wheeled vehicle. The modern shape comes from cursive writing of the traditional character.

relationships.text: 车 is the modern simplified form derived from cursive 車.
